findings.title: Recreate-upgrade exit code changed from 4 to 3 without checking consumers
findings.body: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE moves from 4 to 3, and the new value 4 is reused for FEATURE_DISABLED. Any script, CI pipeline or operator code that treated exit code 4 as 'recreate required' will now read 4 as 'feature disabled'. Callers that already handle 3 will now take the recreate branch. The operator's handling of these exit codes is not part of this diff, so it is unclear whether it was updated. The docs table already listed 3 as the recreate code, which suggests it was out of sync, but this still silently changes a contract that scripts may rely on.

findings.title: Custom image now always bakes in the preview feature rolling-updates
findings.body: `--features=rolling-updates` is added unconditionally to the custom image build. Every test that uses this image, including those that do not use rolling updates, now runs with a build-time preview feature enabled. This hides cases where the feature is off. If the feature is later renamed or removed, `kc.sh build` fails for all of these tests. A build-time feature also makes the operator CR's `features.enabled` list redundant or conflicting for this image.

findings.title: Feature-disabled check runs before config validation and does not stop the command
findings.body: `picocli.exit(...)` followed by `return` relies on exit() recording the code without terminating execution. The check is also placed before `validateConfig()`, so with the feature disabled, invalid arguments such as a missing `--file` on `check` return exit code 4 instead of the usage error 2. The same logic is duplicated in UpdateCompatibilityCheck. A shared guard in AbstractUpdatesCommand would be safer. The test only asserts the error text for the disabled case, not the exit code 4.

findings.title: Docs macro appends --features after parameters, making the example order inconsistent and hiding the requirement
findings.body: The `updatecompatibility` macro now always appends `--features=rolling-updates` to every rendered example. Readers copy the flag without being told why. It is also not a build-time option, so the example mixes build and runtime semantics. The macro does not produce the same text as the CAUTION block describes, and `--features` is emitted after subcommand options, which is unusual. The guide should explain the flag explicitly.

findings.title: Feature-disabled test does not verify exit code and only covers one subcommand
findings.body: `testFeatureNotEnabled` only launches `metadata` and checks the error message. It does not assert the new exit code 4. It does not cover the `check` subcommand, which has the same new guard. The documented contract (exit code 4) is therefore untested.
